Merge Data: Country Name Matching

Objective: Match conflict event data (UCDP) to migration and map data using country names.

  • Aggregate UCDP Data conflict event data by country.
  • Standardize Country Names, remove inconsistencies.
  • Perform the Merge: Use left_join() to merge the conflict data with the migration and map data based on the standardized country names.
  • Inspect the country column in both datasets.

Fuzzy matching

Does not really help much here, but can be very useful in other cases:

Use approximate (fuzzy) matching to align country names when there are minor differences (e.g., “US” vs. “USA”).

  • Identify Unmatched Names: Check which country names in the UCDP data did not match with the map data.
  • Apply Fuzzy Matching: Use string distance measures to find closest matches.
  • Review and Adjust Matches: Manually inspect the results to see potential matches

Spatial Join: Using Geometries for Matching

Match conflict events to countries based on their spatial locations instead of country names.

  • Prepare Spatial Data: Ensure both the UCDP conflict events and map data are in the same coordinate reference system (CRS).
  • Perform Spatial Join: Use st_intersects() or similar spatial functions to assign conflict events to the country polygons they fall within.

Figure 6: Conflict events per country, based on modern borders and spatial join. Unmatched events are shown in purple.

Comparison of Merging Approaches

Approach Use Case Challenges
Name Matching When datasets have consistent country names Requires manual cleaning of names
Fuzzy Matching When names are similar but not identical May produce inaccurate matches
Spatial Join When spatial data is available Computationally intensive for large datasets

(Take-home) Assignment

  • Start a new project for RevealJS (optional also PDF) slides
  • Make a static map of subnational migration patterns in “your” country based on Niva et al. (2023)
  • Add UCDP GED conflict event data to the map
  • Add an interactive leaflet map
  • Calculate aggregates for conflict events on adm1-level and merge the result with the migration data. Make sure that all regions are matched correctly.
  • Produce a matched panel data set on adm2-year level (perform a spatial join if necessary)
  • Adjust the RevealJS slides according to your preferences (use custom themes or modify the custom.scss file)
  • Submit your HTML file and the qmd file used to generate it until Novemer 20, 2024 (email/ILIAS).
